title: Prefix hit-rate counterfactuals & safe TTL tuner
creator: Asha R. Patel
description: Build a small counterfactual simulation and gradual-tuner workflow that produces per-prefix TTL recommendations and a safe, staged apply/rollback plan. The goal is to automate conservative TTL changes that reduce token count and cost while keeping inference latency and model-quality regressions within defined SLO windows. This ticket covers: (1) a sampled trace-based hit-rate simulator that can run counterfactual TTL policies, (2) a percentile-based TTL suggestion engine that targets cost/latency/cava trade-offs, and (3) a staged rollout orchestration with automated safety gates and rollback hooks integrated with Console and the runtime deployment API.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest real KV access traces from production sampling (1M requests sample) and simulate TTL policies offline within 2 hours.
TTL tuner produces per-prefix suggestions with expected hit-rate delta and expected cost savings for 90th/50th/10th percentiles.
Safe rollout plan includes shadow dry-run, 1% canary with latency/cost alarms, 10% gradual ramp with automatic rollback if thresholds breached, and a one-click abort in Console.
End-to-end test: apply suggested TTLs to a dedicated staging cluster and demonstrate <=3% increase in 95th tail latency and >=10% net token cost reduction for the sampled workload.
Documentation describing algorithm, config schema, and runbook for oncall engineers published to Confluence.
implementation_plan: 1) Data: add a trace extractor job (kvt-trace-exporter) that writes sampled prefix hits to internal S3 path (s3://redwood-kv-traces/2026-02).
2) Simulator: implement a single-node simulator that replays traces and supports pluggable TTL policies (fixed, percentile-based, adaptive decay).
3) Tuner: build a batch job that runs candidate TTL vectors and ranks by cost reduction / latency risk using a small econometric model (elastic net on prefix features).

4) Rollout: add rollout state machine in the Console backend that supports: dry-run (shadow), canary (traffic shaping), ramp (step increases), watchdog (metrics-based rollback), and abort hooks tied to runtime API.
5) Safety: add default alarms: model_quality_regressions (eval set match rate drop >2%), latency_95_increase >5ms, error_rate_increase >0.1%.
6) Docs & PR: publish runbook, include CLI helper, and create a GH PR linking to runtime change (GH-rt-1124).
7) Rollout pilot on a non-critical tenant and monitor for 7 days before wider opt-in.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive TTLs increase cache churn and backend load. Mitigation: conservative initial suggestions; cap TTL delta to 3x or absolute lower bound 30s depending on prefix class.

Risk: Silent model-quality regressions when cached prefixes are used in generation. Mitigation: run prompt-level evals on a small held-out set in shadow mode and include a match-rate metric in the watchdog.

Risk: Simulation mismatch vs production due to sampling bias. Mitigation: run multiple replicate samples, expose confidence intervals (bootstrap) and require lower bound of expected savings > threshold before apply.
Risk: Operational complexity in rollback. Mitigation: one-click abort in Console and automated reverse-policy apply that restores previous TTLs and flags an incident.
decisions: Use sampled trace approach rather than full-stream offline replay to reduce infra cost; sampling rate initially 0.5% and adjustable.
Percentile-based TTL suggestions (p90/p50/p10) will be presented; operators choose target sensitivity (conservative/medium/aggressive).
Use bootstrap confidence intervals to express uncertainty; recommendations must pass a >=75% probability of positive net savings to be eligible for automated ramping.

qa_steps: 1) Run simulator locally with sample file: scripts/simulate --input s3://redwood-kv-traces/2026-02/sample.json --policy p90:60s --output /tmp/sim-results.json
2) Validate results: compare simulator hit-rate with production replay for the same sample (tolerance <=10%).
3) Apply to staging via Console and observe the 95th latency and error rates for 24h before canary promotion.
4) Trigger a forced rollback and confirm previous TTLs are re-applied and metrics return to baseline within expected convergence window.
